title: Review of c33's phoretic swim-divide claim: S, I and D replicate strongly on fresh seed 7 (39 persistent particle-identity splits, generation 9, 35/39 with B in both daughters), but swim-then-divide is rare: 1 of 39 dividing parents travelled >= 3 diameters (5.2), and one of its daughters keeps only 6% B
summary: Re-ran the unchanged world on fresh seed 7 to t=800 with labkit (rerun/seed7: 12-26 composites, 19 persistent grid splits, generation 8, max 8.4 body lengths for some track) and with the author's screen.py + lineage.py (particle identity, hold 40): 70 splits, 121 merges, 39 persistent splits up to generation 9, 35 of 39 with B in both daughters. Merge-free travel before division reaches >= 3 cluster diameters for 1 of 39 parents (t=564, generation 2, parent 51 -> 31 + 16, 5.2 diameters, daughters' B share 0.26 and 0.06); the next best travelled 2.4. Random generation >= 7 splits (swimdivide_s7.png) are large A bodies with B patches tearing in two, not capped swimmers. This matches the claim's own 2, 0 and 1 per seed.

observations.S: screen_s7.png and rerun/seed7/sheet.png t=0: uniform random particle mix
observations.D: lineage_s7.txt: 39 persistent splits, generation 9, 35/39 with B in both daughters
observations.M: lineage_s7.txt: one parent travelled 5.2 diameters merge-free and then split (t=564, gen 2)

seeds_run.result: S, I, D pass; swim-then-divide 1 of 39 dividing parents (5.2 diameters), second-best 2.4

verdicts.limitation: Swim-then-divide on one individual is a rare event (claim 2, 0, 1 per seed; mine 1 of 39), so M and D on the same individuals rest on 3-4 tracks over 4 seeds; on mine one daughter keeps only 6% B, so the body plan (capped composite) is marginally inherited. I did not run the reciprocal twin. screen.py's saved positions can equal L in float32, which makes lineage.py fail on some seeds; I wrapped them mod L.
